record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Let D be a finite digraph with n vertices and minimum out-degree k. Must D contain a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/k)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 Every digraph of minimum out-degree k and order n has a cycle of length at most ⌈ n k ⌉.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $D$ be a finite digraph (no loops, at most one arc in each direction between any two vertices is not assumed, but parallel arcs in the same direction are disallowed) on $n$ vertices such that every vertex has out-degree at least $k$, where $k \geq 1$ is an integer. Prove or disprove: $D$ must contain a directed cycle of length at most $\lceil n/k \rceil$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture remains open in general. It is known to hold for k ≤ 5 (k=2 by Caccetta–Häggkvist, k=3 by Hamidoune, k=4 and k=5 by Hoàng–Reed), and Shen proved it whenever k ≤ √(n/2). For the famous k=3 (triangle) case, bounds have been progressively improved (e.g., via flag algebras to about 0.3388n) but the conjecture itself is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Caccetta-Häggkvist Conjecture | Open Problem Garden
status_evidence.snippet: One of the most famous conjectures in graph theory; still open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Caccetta-Häggkvist Conjecture (West's open problems page)
status_evidence.snippet: Proven for r=2,3,4,5; Shen proved it for r ≤ √(n/2).
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for small minimum out-degree and under size assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Rainbow triangles and the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study the k=3 case using flag algebras, improving bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues; the triangle case remains open.
